extractor.note: Partial pass over § 5, where the three basic pieces of the phenomenological method are stated and Heidegger's reduction is expressly distinguished from Husserl's.

coverage_note: Covers § 5, 'The Methodical Character of Ontology. The Three Basic Pieces of the Phenomenological Method'. The rest of the course is not covered.

units.claim: The first basic piece of the method is named the phenomenological reduction, the leading-back of the investigating gaze from the naively grasped being to being.
units.quote: We name this basic piece of the phenomenological method — in the sense of the leading-back of the investigating gaze from the naively grasped being to being — the *phenomenological reduction*.

units.claim: The term is taken over from Husserl in wording but not in the matter: his reduction leads back from the natural attitude to the transcendental life of consciousness.
units.quote: In so doing we link up — in wording, but not in the matter — with a central term of Husserl's phenomenology.

units.claim: Here the reduction leads the gaze back from any determinate grasping of a being to the understanding of the being of that being, projected upon its unconcealedness.
units.quote: the phenomenological reduction means the leading-back of the phenomenological gaze from whatever determinate grasping of a being to the *understanding of the being* (the projection upon the manner of the being's unconcealedness) of this being

units.claim: The reduction is not the central piece, since the turning-away from beings needs the positive projecting of the pre-given being onto its being, which is called phenomenological construction.
units.quote: This projecting of the pre-given being onto its being and its structures we designate as the *phenomenological construction* (phänomenologische Konstruktion).

units.claim: To the reductive construction of being there necessarily belongs a Destruktion, a critical dismantling of the inherited concepts back to the sources from which they were drawn.
units.quote: a *Destruktion*, that is, a *critical dismantling* (kritischer Abbau) of the inherited and initially necessarily-to-be-used concepts back to the sources from which they have been drawn

units.claim: The phenomenological method grows and changes with the advance to the matters, and ceases to be itself as soon as it becomes a technique.
units.quote: *Scientific method is never a technique.* As soon as it becomes that, it has fallen away from its own essence.
